title: The Three Icons in the Righteous Man — Pneumatic, Psychic, Somatic
arc: The teaching names three discrete likenesses that exist in the elect — pneumatic, psychic, somatic — and traces the daily descent of the Living Soul through them in eating and the daily ascent through them in purification, until the Virgin of Light leads her into the icon of the Indweller and seals her in all the members of the New Man.
reading:
This chapter sets out the human in three discrete degrees and then describes the daily cycle of purification that moves the soul down through them and back up through them. The three icons are the pneumatic, the psychic, and the somatic — the spiritual, the intermediate, and the bodily — and they are not three names for one thing but three distinct levels of life within the righteous man, each with its own inhabitants and its own work.

The first icon is the pneumatic, which is the New Man. In her the Mind of Light fashions himself a dwelling and goes inward to abide. This is the inmost degree, where illumined rational understanding takes shape as a living indweller. The second icon is the psychic, called here the residue and remainder of the New Man — the mediating soul-state that is bound into the flesh and so coincides with the Old Man for the duration of bodily life. The third icon is the somatic, the body itself, which contains both the others as their outermost vessel and so is described as the icon "which contains them all." The teaching is careful to keep these as discrete degrees: the pneumatic is the seat of the Indweller, the psychic is the mingled middle bound to flesh, the somatic is the outermost containing form.

Across these three runs a daily motion. Through the food of eating the Living Soul sinks downward from her higher seat, is poured into the somatic, and is set there in the icon of the body. Then, as she is conveyed upward again, she falls back into the psychic icon, where she is poured among the enemies — the wraths, desires, and the other corrupt affections that are mingled with her in that middle degree. This is the cosmic-mingled state lived out within a single human day: the soul is continually drawn down into ultimates by the bodily intake and continually drawn up again, and on each return she must pass through the territory of the proprium where bitterness, desire, foolishness, envy, discord, and evil teachings press in on her.

The work of regeneration is shown as a separating-forth performed at each of the three levels. In the somatic icon the Living Soul releases the body itself, which is not hers. In the psychic she releases the fortunes that are not hers — the bitterness, the desire, foolishness, envy, discord, and the other evil teachings mingled with her there. Only in the pneumatic icon does she not release but live and join inward: there she is conjoined with patience, the perfection of faith, and with agape, which is queen over them all. The downward arc passes through clothing in flesh; the upward arc passes through stripping off what is not hers; the inmost arc is conjunction.

The agent of this ascent is the Virgin of Light. When the soul has been brought into the psychic and is hard-pressed by the enemies, the Virgin reveals herself to her, blazes a path, travels before her inward, and draws her up to the height — into the icon of the Indweller, the New Man. There the New Man adorns her, and she takes the seal in all the members of the Virgin of Light who dwells in him. The Virgin is named here as the robe of the New Man — the uncorrupted purity of reception that the regenerate self wears — and she is also given the title "the hour of life," the soul that is at once first and last, the inmost and the consummating. The "seal in all the members" is the imprint of confirmed correspondence: every faculty of the regenerate organism receives the mark of conjunction.

The teaching closes by widening the picture from the single righteous man to the universal pattern. The Living Member is continually redeemed from every life and comes into the body of the Righteous one outside, in the dispensation of prophecy. The same type holds in the All: the Living Soul is purified every day, crossing through these three icons — releasing the body that is not hers in the somatic, releasing the mingled affections that are not hers in the psychic, and living and joining inward in the pneumatic with patience, faith, and love. The three discrete degrees of the human are thus disclosed as the daily theatre of redemption itself, and the Virgin of Light is the queen-principle by whom the Living Soul is conducted home through them.
